issues.legal_issue: In a specific-performance suit, the burden of establishing that a subsequent purchaser acted in good faith without notice of the earlier agreement rests on the purchaser asserting that defense.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought specific performance of an earlier agreement to sell the property.
The appellants had subsequently purchased the property and asserted that they were bona fide purchasers without notice of the earlier agreement.
issues.conclusion: The burden of proving that they were bona fide purchasers without notice rested on the appellants, and they did not discharge it in the circumstances of the case.
issues.legal_principle: The Court placed the burden on the purchasers who relied on their status as bona fide purchasers without notice and assessed whether they had discharged it in light of the evidence and circumstances. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.subsequent_purchasers: The persons resisting specific performance acquired the property after the agreement at issue.
predicates.purchasers_claim_good_faith_without_noti: The subsequent purchasers assert that they acquired the property in good faith without notice of the earlier agreement.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns property acquired later by purchasers who claim good faith without notice, those purchasers bear the burden of establishing that claim.

issues.legal_issue: Subsequent purchasers who had notice of an earlier agreement to sell were not bona fide purchasers without notice and could not defeat specific performance on that basis.
material_facts: The plaintiff had an agreement to purchase the property before the appellants acquired it.
Evidence supported the finding that one appellant was told of the earlier agreement when it was made.
Evidence also supported the finding that the appellants measured the property and were warned that it had already been agreed to be sold.
The parties conducted business in the same vicinity, and the sale to the appellants was arranged and completed unusually quickly.
The appellants denied knowledge of the earlier agreement and denied measuring the property.
issues.conclusion: The Court accepted the evidence that the appellants had notice of the earlier agreement, held that they had not established that they were bona fide purchasers without notice, and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Whether purchasers had notice and discharged their burden is determined from the evidence and the circumstances of the transaction. The Court relied on the testimony about communication of the earlier agreement and the warning during measurement, considered alongside the parties' proximity and the haste of the sale. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this assessment.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and subsequent_purchase and (agreement_notice_communicated_to_buyer or (property_measured_after_prior_agreement and buyer_warned_of_prior_agreement and local_business_proximity and rapid_conveyance))

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.subsequent_purchase: The purchaser acquired the property after the agreement at issue.
predicates.agreement_notice_communicated_to_buyer: A witness reported that the purchaser was told that the property had already been agreed to be sold.
predicates.property_measured_after_prior_agreement: The purchaser measured the property after the earlier agreement had been made.
predicates.buyer_warned_of_prior_agreement: Someone warned the purchaser during the measurement that the property had already been agreed to be sold.
predicates.local_business_proximity: The parties lived or conducted business in close proximity to one another.
predicates.rapid_conveyance: The sale was arranged and completed unusually quickly.

issues.definition: Where a subsequent purchase in a specific-performance suit is accompanied by communicated notice, or by post-agreement measurement and warning together with local proximity and a rapid sale, the purchasers had notice and cannot claim good faith without notice.
